newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares continue slide in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares continue slide in slow trade.

text.p: Commerical International Bank (CIB) domintated trading for the second day on Cairo's stock market on Tuesday but most shares prices closed lower.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index fell 5.15 points to 352.54 while volume was 70.96 million pounds ($20.90 million).
Almost five million pounds of that volume was generated through the sale to the public of 177,778 shares at 28 pounds per share in National Bank for Development (NBD).
NBD made 30.9 million pounds profit in 1996, up from 24.669 million pounds in 1995. It had shareholders' equity worth 242.8 million pounds in 1996, up from 152.717 million pounds.

"The market continued to drop today as expected. It was a very bad day for the stock exchange, there was almost panic because most prices went down," said Mohammed Abdullah, managing director of Intercapital.
"There is no fundamental reason behind the drop. But we expect prices to pick up by next week," he added.

Abdullah said the government's decision this week to offer for sale to the public shares worth 1.5 billion pounds ($440 million) in the strategic sugar, aluminium and steel industries through the stock exchange would encourage foreign investors to return to the Cairo market in earnet.
CIB topped the day's list of most active shares, rising 1.5 pounds to close at 71.5 after trade worth 8.96 million pounds.
"People are taking advantage of the difference between the Global Depositary Receipt and the local price. The GDR is higher so it's cheaper here," Abdullah said.
Shares worth 5.71 million pounds were traded in North Cairo Flour Mills but it ended unchanged at 169 pounds. All other mills slipped in price.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills lsot 4.07 to close at 77.35 after trade in 3.49 million pounds. Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 3.09 pounds lower at 75 after shares worth 2.69 changed hands.
"The mills dragged the whole market down. But at their current low prices they may start to be attrative again," Abdullah said.
Suez Cement was the only stock in its sector to rise, closing 2.76 pounds higher at 65 after trade in 4.70 million pounds.
"This was not a fair closing price because the stock opened at 60 and was trading at that price and at 61 for most of the day," Abdullah said.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 497.26 points from 504.89 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms fell to 256.83 from 260.49.
Out of the 84 shares traded, 16 ended up, 48 fell and 20 were unchanged
